import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Green's conjecture

Green's conjecture states that the Clifford index of a non-hyperelliptic curve over $\mathbb{C}$
is determined by the extent to which the curve, as a canonical curve, has linear syzygies.

A smooth projective curve $C$ over $\mathbb{C}$ is determined up to isomorphism by its function
field $F$, an algebraic function field of one variable over $\mathbb{C}$ (a finite extension of
$\mathbb{C}(t)$). Following Stichtenoth's textbook [St09], we model $C$ by $F$: the points of $C$
are the places of $F$ (valuation subrings $\mathbb{C} \subseteq \mathcal{O} \subsetneq F$),
divisors are finite formal $\mathbb{Z}$-linear combinations of places, $\mathcal{L}(D)$ is the
Riemann–Roch space of a divisor $D$ and $\ell(D)$ its dimension, the genus is
$g = \max_D (\deg D - \ell(D) + 1)$ (Riemann's theorem), and a canonical divisor is a divisor $K$
with $\deg K = 2g - 2$ and $\ell(K) \ge g$.

For a smooth projective non-hyperelliptic curve of genus $g \ge 4$, the *Clifford index* is
$$\operatorname{Cliff}(C) = \min\{\deg D - 2(\ell(D) - 1) : h^0(D) \ge 2,\ h^1(D) \ge 2\}.$$
The canonical curve $C \subseteq \mathbb{P}^{g-1}$ is projectively normal (Noether), so its
homogeneous coordinate ring is the canonical ring $\bigoplus_q H^0(C, qK)$, and its graded
Betti numbers are $\beta_{p, p+q} = \dim K_{p,q}(C, K_C)$, where the Koszul cohomology group
$K_{p,q}(C, K_C)$ is the middle cohomology of
$$\bigwedge^{p+1} V \otimes H^0(C, (q-1)K) \to \bigwedge^{p} V \otimes H^0(C, qK)
  \to \bigwedge^{p-1} V \otimes H^0(C, (q+1)K), \qquad V = H^0(C, K).$$
We realise this Koszul complex inside the exterior algebra
$\bigwedge_F (F \otimes_{\mathbb{C}} V)$, whose differential is the contraction against the
$F$-linear form $F \otimes_{\mathbb{C}} V \to F$, $f \otimes v \mapsto f v$.

Green's conjecture states $\operatorname{Cliff}(C) = \min\{p : K_{p,2}(C, K_C) \neq 0\}$,
i.e. $\beta_{p, p+2} = 0$ exactly for $p < \operatorname{Cliff}(C)$ (in the range $p \le g - 3$
where the Betti table is nontrivial). The inequality
$\min\{p : K_{p,2}(C, K_C) \ne 0\} \le \operatorname{Cliff}(C)$ is the Green–Lazarsfeld
nonvanishing theorem; the reverse inequality is open. Voisin proved the conjecture for generic
curves.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Green's conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green%27s_conjecture)
- [Gr84] M. Green, *Koszul cohomology and the geometry of projective varieties*,
  J. Differential Geom. 19 (1984), 125–171.
- [St09] H. Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, 2nd ed., Springer GTM 254, 2009.
-/
open scoped TensorProduct
namespace GreensConjecture
variable (F : Type*) [Field F] [Algebra ℂ F]

blocks.docstring:
A *place* of the function field `F` over `ℂ`, i.e. a closed point of the corresponding
smooth projective curve: a valuation subring `𝒪 ⊊ F` containing `ℂ` (see [St09, Section 1.1]).
Such a valuation ring is automatically a discrete valuation ring with residue field `ℂ`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: ValuationSubring F (used as the carrier), IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (only covers an affine model, misses points at infinity), AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme (no smooth projective curve API, no cohomology).
justification.name: GreensConjecture.Place
justification.why_needed: Closed points of a smooth projective curve over ℂ; Mathlib has no curves/points of function fields.

  __ := P.toValuationSubring.toSubring

blocks.docstring:
`t : F` is a *uniformizer* (local parameter) at `P` if it generates the maximal ideal of
the valuation ring of `P`, i.e. `v_P(t) = 1`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: IsDiscreteValuationRing / Irreducible (would need a DVR instance we cannot supply without proof); IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.valuation (wrong setting).

blocks.name: IsUniformizer
blocks.text:
/-- `t : F` is a *uniformizer* (local parameter) at `P` if it generates the maximal ideal of
the valuation ring of `P`, i.e. `v_P(t) = 1`. -/
def IsUniformizer (P : Place F) (t : F) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : t ∈ P.toValuationSubring,
    Ideal.span {(⟨t, h⟩ : P.toValuationSubring)} = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal P.toValuationSubring
end Place

blocks.docstring:
The Riemann–Roch space `𝓛(D) = {f ∈ F | v_P(f) ≥ -D(P) for all places P}` of a divisor `D`,
as a `ℂ`-subspace of `F`. The condition `v_P(f) ≥ -D(P)` is expressed as `t ^ D(P) * f ∈ 𝒪_P` for
every uniformizer `t` at `P` (see [St09, Section 1.4]).

justification.closest_existing_considered: CategoryTheory.Sites.SheafCohomology (abstract, no curves/line bundles), AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules (no invertible sheaves/cohomology API).
justification.name: GreensConjecture.Divisor.riemannRochSpace
justification.why_needed: H^0(C, 𝒪(D)) = 𝓛(D); no sheaf cohomology / line bundles on curves in Mathlib.

blocks.name: riemannRochSpace
blocks.text:
/-- The Riemann–Roch space `𝓛(D) = {f ∈ F | v_P(f) ≥ -D(P) for all places P}` of a divisor `D`,
as a `ℂ`-subspace of `F`. The condition `v_P(f) ≥ -D(P)` is expressed as `t ^ D(P) * f ∈ 𝒪_P` for
every uniformizer `t` at `P` (see [St09, Section 1.4]). -/
def riemannRochSpace (D : Divisor F) : Submodule ℂ F :=
  ⨅ (P : Place F) (t : F) (_ : P.IsUniformizer t),
    (Subalgebra.toSubmodule P.toSubalgebra).comap (LinearMap.mulLeft ℂ (t ^ D P))

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem algebraMap_mem_riemannRochSpace_zero (c : ℂ) :
    algebraMap ℂ F c ∈ (0 : Divisor F).riemannRochSpace := by
  simp only [Divisor.riemannRochSpace, Submodule.mem_iInf, Submodule.mem_comap,
    LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, Finsupp.coe_zero, Pi.zero_apply, zpow_zero, one_mul,
    Subalgebra.mem_toSubmodule]
  intro P t _
  exact P.toSubalgebra.algebraMap_mem c

blocks.text:

noncomputable def ell (D : Divisor F) : ℕ := Module.finrank ℂ D.riemannRochSpace

blocks.code:
noncomputable def genus : ℕ :=
  sSup {g : ℕ | ∃ D : Divisor F, (g : ℤ) = D.deg - D.ell + 1}
blocks.docstring:
The genus of the curve with function field `F`, defined via Riemann's theorem as
`g = max {deg D - ℓ(D) + 1 | D a divisor}` (see [St09, Section 1.4]).

justification.name: GreensConjecture.genus
justification.why_needed: Genus of the curve; absent from Mathlib.

blocks.name: genus
blocks.text:
/-- The genus of the curve with function field `F`, defined via Riemann's theorem as
`g = max {deg D - ℓ(D) + 1 | D a divisor}` (see [St09, Section 1.4]). -/
noncomputable def genus : ℕ :=
  sSup {g : ℕ | ∃ D : Divisor F, (g : ℤ) = D.deg - D.ell + 1}
variable {F}

blocks.code:
noncomputable def indexOfSpeciality (D : Divisor F) : ℤ :=
  D.ell - D.deg + genus F - 1
blocks.docstring:
The index of speciality `i(D) = ℓ(D) - deg D + g - 1` of a divisor `D`; by the Riemann–Roch
theorem this is `h^1(C, 𝒪(D)) = ℓ(K - D)` for a canonical divisor `K`
(see [St09, Sections 1.5, 1.6]).

justification.name: GreensConjecture.indexOfSpeciality
justification.why_needed: h^1(C, 𝒪(D)) via Riemann–Roch, needed for the Clifford index.

blocks.name: indexOfSpeciality
blocks.text:
/-- The index of speciality `i(D) = ℓ(D) - deg D + g - 1` of a divisor `D`; by the Riemann–Roch
theorem this is `h^1(C, 𝒪(D)) = ℓ(K - D)` for a canonical divisor `K`
(see [St09, Sections 1.5, 1.6]). -/
noncomputable def indexOfSpeciality (D : Divisor F) : ℤ :=
  D.ell - D.deg + genus F - 1

blocks.code:
def IsCanonical (K : Divisor F) : Prop :=
  K.deg = 2 * (genus F : ℤ) - 2 ∧ genus F ≤ K.ell
blocks.docstring:
A divisor `K` is *canonical* if `deg K = 2g - 2` and `ℓ(K) ≥ g`; equivalently, `K` is the
divisor of a nonzero rational differential on the curve (see [St09, Section 1.6]).

justification.closest_existing_considered: KaehlerDifferential ℂ F (would require finite-support proofs to build the divisor of a differential); numerical characterisation used instead.
justification.name: GreensConjecture.IsCanonical
justification.why_needed: Canonical divisor K_C; no canonical sheaf/divisor in Mathlib.

blocks.name: IsCanonical
blocks.text:
/-- A divisor `K` is *canonical* if `deg K = 2g - 2` and `ℓ(K) ≥ g`; equivalently, `K` is the
divisor of a nonzero rational differential on the curve (see [St09, Section 1.6]). -/
def IsCanonical (K : Divisor F) : Prop :=
  K.deg = 2 * (genus F : ℤ) - 2 ∧ genus F ≤ K.ell

blocks.code:
def IsHyperelliptic : Prop :=
  2 ≤ genus F ∧ ∃ D : Divisor F, D.deg = 2 ∧ D.ell = 2
blocks.docstring:
The curve is *hyperelliptic* if it has genus `g ≥ 2` and admits a divisor `D` with
`deg D = 2` and `ℓ(D) = 2`, i.e. a degree two map to `ℙ¹` (see [St09, Section 6.2]).

justification.name: GreensConjecture.IsHyperelliptic
justification.why_needed: Hypothesis of the conjecture; absent from Mathlib.

blocks.name: IsHyperelliptic
blocks.text:
variable (F) in
/-- The curve is *hyperelliptic* if it has genus `g ≥ 2` and admits a divisor `D` with
`deg D = 2` and `ℓ(D) = 2`, i.e. a degree two map to `ℙ¹` (see [St09, Section 6.2]). -/
def IsHyperelliptic : Prop :=
  2 ≤ genus F ∧ ∃ D : Divisor F, D.deg = 2 ∧ D.ell = 2

blocks.docstring:
The *Clifford index* of the curve with function field `F` (of genus `g ≥ 4`):
`Cliff(C) = min {deg D - 2 (ℓ(D) - 1) | h^0(D) ≥ 2 and h^1(D) ≥ 2}`, where `h^0(D) = ℓ(D)` and
`h^1(D) = i(D)` is the index of speciality. By Clifford's theorem each such
`deg D - 2 (ℓ(D) - 1)` is a nonnegative integer.

justification.name: GreensConjecture.cliffordIndex
justification.why_needed: Clifford index of the curve; absent from Mathlib.

blocks.name: cliffordIndex
blocks.text:
variable (F) in
/-- The *Clifford index* of the curve with function field `F` (of genus `g ≥ 4`):
`Cliff(C) = min {deg D - 2 (ℓ(D) - 1) | h^0(D) ≥ 2 and h^1(D) ≥ 2}`, where `h^0(D) = ℓ(D)` and
`h^1(D) = i(D)` is the index of speciality. By Clifford's theorem each such
`deg D - 2 (ℓ(D) - 1)` is a nonnegative integer. -/
noncomputable def cliffordIndex : ℕ :=
  sInf {c : ℕ | ∃ D : Divisor F, 2 ≤ D.ell ∧ 2 ≤ indexOfSpeciality D ∧
    (c : ℤ) = D.deg - 2 * (D.ell - 1)}

blocks.code:
abbrev KoszulSpace (K : Divisor F) :=
  ExteriorAlgebra F (F ⊗[ℂ] K.riemannRochSpace)
blocks.docstring:
The exterior algebra `⋀_F (F ⊗_ℂ V)` with `V = 𝓛(K)`; the Koszul complex computing the Koszul
cohomology groups `K_{p,q}(C, K)` lives inside it.

justification.name: GreensConjecture.KoszulSpace
justification.why_needed: Ambient exterior algebra ⋀_F(F ⊗_ℂ 𝓛(K)) housing the Koszul complex.

blocks.name: KoszulSpace
blocks.text:
/-- The exterior algebra `⋀_F (F ⊗_ℂ V)` with `V = 𝓛(K)`; the Koszul complex computing the Koszul
cohomology groups `K_{p,q}(C, K)` lives inside it. -/
abbrev KoszulSpace (K : Divisor F) :=
  ExteriorAlgebra F (F ⊗[ℂ] K.riemannRochSpace)

blocks.code:
noncomputable def koszulDifferential (K : Divisor F) : KoszulSpace K →ₗ[ℂ] KoszulSpace K :=
  (CliffordAlgebra.contractLeft (Q := (0 : QuadraticForm F (F ⊗[ℂ] K.riemannRochSpace)))
    (K.riemannRochSpace.subtype.liftBaseChange F)).restrictScalars ℂ
blocks.docstring:
The Koszul differential: contraction against the `F`-linear form
`F ⊗_ℂ 𝓛(K) → F`, `f ⊗ v ↦ f v`. On `w • (v₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ vₙ)` it is
`∑ᵢ (-1)^(i+1) (vᵢ w) • (v₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ v̂ᵢ ∧ ⋯ ∧ vₙ)`.

justification.name: GreensConjecture.koszulDifferential
justification.why_needed: Koszul differential; Mathlib has no Koszul complex or graded Tor/Betti numbers.

blocks.name: koszulDifferential
blocks.text:
/-- The Koszul differential: contraction against the `F`-linear form
`F ⊗_ℂ 𝓛(K) → F`, `f ⊗ v ↦ f v`. On `w • (v₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ vₙ)` it is
`∑ᵢ (-1)^(i+1) (vᵢ w) • (v₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ v̂ᵢ ∧ ⋯ ∧ vₙ)`. -/
noncomputable def koszulDifferential (K : Divisor F) : KoszulSpace K →ₗ[ℂ] KoszulSpace K :=
  (CliffordAlgebra.contractLeft (Q := (0 : QuadraticForm F (F ⊗[ℂ] K.riemannRochSpace)))
    (K.riemannRochSpace.subtype.liftBaseChange F)).restrictScalars ℂ

blocks.docstring:
The bigraded piece `⋀^p V ⊗_ℂ W` of the Koszul complex, for `V = 𝓛(K)` and a `ℂ`-subspace
`W ⊆ F`: the `ℂ`-span of the elements `w • (v₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ vₚ)` with `w ∈ W` and `vᵢ ∈ V`.

justification.name: GreensConjecture.koszulPiece
justification.why_needed: Bigraded piece ⋀^p V ⊗ 𝓛(qK) of the Koszul complex.

blocks.name: koszulPiece

blocks.docstring:
The Koszul cohomology group `K_{p,q}(C, K)` vanishes: the cycles in `⋀^p V ⊗ 𝓛(qK)` are
exactly the boundaries of `⋀^(p+1) V ⊗ 𝓛((q-1)K)`, where `V = 𝓛(K)`. When `K` is canonical
and the curve is non-hyperelliptic, `K_{p,q}(C, K) = 0` means that the graded Betti number
`β_{p,p+q}` of the canonical curve vanishes.

justification.closest_existing_considered: No graded Betti numbers, minimal free resolutions or Koszul cohomology in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib.
justification.name: GreensConjecture.KoszulCohomologyVanishes
justification.why_needed: K_{p,q}(C, K_C) = 0, i.e. vanishing of the graded Betti number β_{p,p+q} of the canonical curve.

blocks.name: KoszulCohomologyVanishes
blocks.text:
/-- The Koszul cohomology group `K_{p,q}(C, K)` vanishes: the cycles in `⋀^p V ⊗ 𝓛(qK)` are
exactly the boundaries of `⋀^(p+1) V ⊗ 𝓛((q-1)K)`, where `V = 𝓛(K)`. When `K` is canonical
and the curve is non-hyperelliptic, `K_{p,q}(C, K) = 0` means that the graded Betti number
`β_{p,p+q}` of the canonical curve vanishes. -/
def KoszulCohomologyVanishes (K : Divisor F) (p q : ℕ) : Prop :=
  LinearMap.ker (koszulDifferential K) ⊓ koszulPiece K p ((q : ℤ) • K).riemannRochSpace =
    (koszulPiece K (p + 1) (((q : ℤ) - 1) • K).riemannRochSpace).map (koszulDifferential K)

blocks.docstring:
**Green's conjecture.** Let $C$ be a smooth projective non-hyperelliptic curve over
$\mathbb{C}$ of genus $g \ge 4$, with function field $F$ and canonical divisor $K$. Then the
Clifford index of $C$ is determined by the linear syzygies of the canonical curve
$C \subseteq \mathbb{P}^{g-1}$:
$$\operatorname{Cliff}(C) = \min\{p : K_{p,2}(C, K_C) \neq 0\},$$
i.e. $K_{p,2}(C, K_C) = 0$ for all $p < \operatorname{Cliff}(C)$ and
$K_{\operatorname{Cliff}(C), 2}(C, K_C) \ne 0$. Equivalently, if $a(C)$ is the largest $i$ such that
the graded Betti numbers $\beta_{p,p+2}$ of the canonical curve vanish for all $p \le i$, then
$\operatorname{Cliff}(C) = a(C) + 1$. The inequality $a(C) + 1 \le \operatorname{Cliff}(C)$ is the
Green–Lazarsfeld nonvanishing theorem; the reverse inequality is the open part.

The hypothesis $g \ge 4$ excludes the degenerate cases: curves of genus $g \le 2$ are
hyperelliptic (or have no canonical embedding), and a non-hyperelliptic curve of genus $3$ is a
plane quartic, for which no divisor computes the Clifford index and $K_{p,2}(C, K_C) = 0$ for
all $p$.

claims.decomposer_note: Per the article this means: for every smooth projective non-hyperelliptic curve C over ℂ (genus g ≥ 3), Cliff(C) = a(C) + 1, where a(C) is the largest i such that the graded Betti numbers β_{p,p+2} of the minimal free resolution of the canonical coordinate ring vanish for all p ≤ i (equivalently K_{p,2}(C,K_C) = 0 ⟺ p < Cliff(C)); the inequality a(C)+1 ≤ Cliff(C) is the proven Green–Lazarsfeld theorem, so the open content is the reverse inequality, and the ground field ℂ, smoothness/projectivity, and the non-hyperelliptic hypothesis (needed for the canonical map to be an embedding) are implicit quantifier restrictions; Voisin's generic-case result is a partial result not posed by the statement.
claims.reviewer_why: c03 states exactly the source's content Cliff(C) = a(C)+1 as `IsLeast {p | K_{p,2}(C,K_C) ≠ 0} (Cliff C)` (no junk values, unlike c07's `ℤ = ↑(sInf ℕ-set)`), for every smooth projective non-hyperelliptic curve over ℂ modelled by its function field (Mathlib's `FunctionField ℂ F`), quantifying over every canonical divisor. I verified each bespoke definition against Stichtenoth: places = valuation subrings ℂ ⊆ 𝒪 ⊊ F (automatically DVRs, degree 1 over ℂ), L(D) via t^{D(P)}·f ∈ 𝒪_P for uniformizers t (checked by simp to unfold as intended), genus via Riemann's theorem as an ℕ-sSup (set nonempty and bounded, so it is the max), canonical divisor via deg = 2g−2 ∧ ℓ ≥ g (Stichtenoth 1.6.2), hyperelliptic via a g¹₂ (ℓ = 2 is equivalent to ℓ ≥ 2 for g ≥ 2, deg 2), Clifford index = min over h⁰ ≥ 2, h¹ ≥ 2 of deg D − 2(ℓ(D)−1) (nonempty for g ≥ 4; values ≥ 0 by Clifford, so the ℕ-cast loses nothing). Koszul cohomology K_{p,q}(C,K_C) is realised inside ⋀_F(F ⊗_ℂ L(K)) with the contraction against f ⊗ v ↦ f·v (checked to be that functional); the bigraded piece is the ℂ-span of w•(1⊗v₁)∧…∧(1⊗vₚ), which is W ⊗ ⋀^p V by base change and injectivity over a field; vanishing = cycles equal boundaries (image ⊆ cycles holds automatically). β_{p,p+2} of the canonical curve equals dim K_{p,2} by Green's theorem plus Noether's projective normality. Index alignment double-checked: GL nonvanishing gives K_{Cliff,2} ≠ 0 via K_{g−2−Cliff,1} ≠ 0 and Green duality; trigonal/plane-quintic cases (Cliff 1, K_{1,2} ≠ 0 by Petri) agree. Genus ≥ 4 (rather than the table's ≥ 3) is required for the equality formulation: for a plane quartic all β_{p,p+2} vanish while Cliff = 1 by convention, so the equality is literally false at g = 3; that case is trivially known and carries no open content. c06 (g ≥ 3 via the nonstandard convention Cliff = ⊤) and c08 (open direction only, g ≥ 3) are also faithful models but match the source's 'equality' wording less directly.

context: In mathematics, Clifford's theorem on special divisors is a result of William K. Clifford (1878) on algebraic curves, showing the constraints on special linear systems on a curve C.

decomposition_objections.text: The notes' precise formulation needs two corrections. (1) The genus range "g ≥ 3": for a non-hyperelliptic genus-3 curve (plane quartic) the canonical ideal is generated by a single quartic, so β_{p,p+2} = 0 for every p; a(C) = "largest i with β_{p,p+2} = 0 for all p ≤ i" is then undefined (infinite), and Cliff(C) = 1 only by convention (no divisor with h^0, h^1 ≥ 2 exists). The equality Cliff(C) = a(C)+1 is therefore only meaningful for g ≥ 4, which is the range I used; the genus-3 case carries no open content. (2) The gloss "K_{p,2}(C,K_C) = 0 ⟺ p < Cliff(C)" cannot hold for all p: K_{p,2}(C,K_C) = 0 for every p ≥ g − 2 (e.g. β_{g−2,g} = 0 by Gorenstein duality) although p ≥ Cliff(C). The correct statement is Cliff(C) = min{p : K_{p,2}(C,K_C) ≠ 0} (equivalently the iff restricted to p ≤ g − 3), which is what `IsLeast` expresses. I otherwise conformed to the table (single slot, equality form including the proven Green–Lazarsfeld half).

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Green's conjecture

Green's conjecture states that the Clifford index of a non-hyperelliptic curve over $\mathbb{C}$
is determined by the extent to which the curve, as a canonical curve, has linear syzygies.

A smooth projective curve $C$ over $\mathbb{C}$ is determined up to isomorphism by its function
field $F$, an algebraic function field of one variable over $\mathbb{C}$ (a finite extension of
$\mathbb{C}(t)$). Following Stichtenoth's textbook [St09], we model $C$ by $F$: the points of $C$
are the places of $F$ (valuation subrings $\mathbb{C} \subseteq \mathcal{O} \subsetneq F$),
divisors are finite formal $\mathbb{Z}$-linear combinations of places, $\mathcal{L}(D)$ is the
Riemann–Roch space of a divisor $D$ and $\ell(D)$ its dimension, the genus is
$g = \max_D (\deg D - \ell(D) + 1)$ (Riemann's theorem), and a canonical divisor is a divisor $K$
with $\deg K = 2g - 2$ and $\ell(K) \ge g$.

For a smooth projective non-hyperelliptic curve of genus $g \ge 4$, the *Clifford index* is
$$\operatorname{Cliff}(C) = \min\{\deg D - 2(\ell(D) - 1) : h^0(D) \ge 2,\ h^1(D) \ge 2\}.$$
The canonical curve $C \subseteq \mathbb{P}^{g-1}$ is projectively normal (Noether), so its
homogeneous coordinate ring is the canonical ring $\bigoplus_q H^0(C, qK)$, and its graded
Betti numbers are $\beta_{p, p+q} = \dim K_{p,q}(C, K_C)$, where the Koszul cohomology group
$K_{p,q}(C, K_C)$ is the middle cohomology of
$$\bigwedge^{p+1} V \otimes H^0(C, (q-1)K) \to \bigwedge^{p} V \otimes H^0(C, qK)
  \to \bigwedge^{p-1} V \otimes H^0(C, (q+1)K), \qquad V = H^0(C, K).$$
We realise this Koszul complex inside the exterior algebra
$\bigwedge_F (F \otimes_{\mathbb{C}} V)$, whose differential is the contraction against the
$F$-linear form $F \otimes_{\mathbb{C}} V \to F$, $f \otimes v \mapsto f v$.

Green's conjecture states $\operatorname{Cliff}(C) = \min\{p : K_{p,2}(C, K_C) \neq 0\}$,
i.e. $\beta_{p, p+2} = 0$ exactly for $p < \operatorname{Cliff}(C)$ (in the range $p \le g - 3$
where the Betti table is nontrivial). The inequality
$\min\{p : K_{p,2}(C, K_C) \ne 0\} \le \operatorname{Cliff}(C)$ is the Green–Lazarsfeld
nonvanishing theorem; the reverse inequality is open. Voisin proved the conjecture for generic
curves.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Green's conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green%27s_conjecture)
- [Gr84] M. Green, *Koszul cohomology and the geometry of projective varieties*,
  J. Differential Geom. 19 (1984), 125–171.
- [St09] H. Stichtenoth, *Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, 2nd ed., Springer GTM 254, 2009.
-/

open scoped TensorProduct

namespace GreensConjecture

variable (F : Type*) [Field F] [Algebra ℂ F]

/-- A *place* of the function field `F` over `ℂ`, i.e. a closed point of the corresponding
smooth projective curve: a valuation subring `𝒪 ⊊ F` containing `ℂ` (see [St09, Section 1.1]).
Such a valuation ring is automatically a discrete valuation ring with residue field `ℂ`. -/
structure Place where
  /-- The valuation ring of the place. -/
  toValuationSubring : ValuationSubring F
  algebraMap_mem : ∀ c : ℂ, algebraMap ℂ F c ∈ toValuationSubring
  ne_top : toValuationSubring ≠ ⊤

namespace Place

variable {F}

/-- The valuation ring of a place, as a `ℂ`-subalgebra of `F`. -/
def toSubalgebra (P : Place F) : Subalgebra ℂ F where
  __ := P.toValuationSubring.toSubring
  algebraMap_mem' := P.algebraMap_mem

/-- `t : F` is a *uniformizer* (local parameter) at `P` if it generates the maximal ideal of
the valuation ring of `P`, i.e. `v_P(t) = 1`. -/
def IsUniformizer (P : Place F) (t : F) : Prop :=
  ∃ h : t ∈ P.toValuationSubring,
    Ideal.span {(⟨t, h⟩ : P.toValuationSubring)} = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal P.toValuationSubring

end Place

/-- A *divisor* on the curve with function field `F`: a finite formal `ℤ`-linear combination of
places. -/
abbrev Divisor := Place F →₀ ℤ

namespace Divisor

variable {F}

/-- The degree of a divisor. Since `ℂ` is algebraically closed every place has degree one, so
the degree of `D` is the sum of its coefficients. -/
def deg (D : Divisor F) : ℤ := D.sum fun _ n => n

@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem deg_zero : (0 : Divisor F).deg = 0 := by
  simp [Divisor.deg]

@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem deg_add (D E : Divisor F) : (D + E).deg = D.deg + E.deg := by
  simp [Divisor.deg, Finsupp.sum_add_index']

@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem deg_neg (D : Divisor F) : (-D).deg = -D.deg := by
  simp [Divisor.deg, Finsupp.sum_neg_index]

@[category API, AMS 14]
theorem deg_single (P : Place F) (n : ℤ) : Divisor.deg (Finsupp.single P n) = n := by
  simp [Divisor.deg]

/-- The Riemann–Roch space `𝓛(D) = {f ∈ F | v_P(f) ≥ -D(P) for all places P}` of a divisor `D`,
as a `ℂ`-subspace of `F`. The condition `v_P(f) ≥ -D(P)` is expressed as `t ^ D(P) * f ∈ 𝒪_P` for
every uniformizer `t` at `P` (see [St09, Section 1.4]). -/
def riemannRochSpace (D : Divisor F) : Submodule ℂ F :=
  ⨅ (P : Place F) (t : F) (_ : P.IsUniformizer t),
    (Subalgebra.toSubmodule P.toSubalgebra).comap (LinearMap.mulLeft ℂ (t ^ D P))

@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem algebraMap_mem_riemannRochSpace_zero (c : ℂ) :
    algebraMap ℂ F c ∈ (0 : Divisor F).riemannRochSpace := by
  simp only [Divisor.riemannRochSpace, Submodule.mem_iInf, Submodule.mem_comap,
    LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, Finsupp.coe_zero, Pi.zero_apply, zpow_zero, one_mul,
    Subalgebra.mem_toSubmodule]
  intro P t _
  exact P.toSubalgebra.algebraMap_mem c

/-- `ℓ(D) = dim_ℂ 𝓛(D)`, the dimension of the Riemann–Roch space of `D`. -/
noncomputable def ell (D : Divisor F) : ℕ := Module.finrank ℂ D.riemannRochSpace

end Divisor

/-- The genus of the curve with function field `F`, defined via Riemann's theorem as
`g = max {deg D - ℓ(D) + 1 | D a divisor}` (see [St09, Section 1.4]). -/
noncomputable def genus : ℕ :=
  sSup {g : ℕ | ∃ D : Divisor F, (g : ℤ) = D.deg - D.ell + 1}

variable {F}

/-- The index of speciality `i(D) = ℓ(D) - deg D + g - 1` of a divisor `D`; by the Riemann–Roch
theorem this is `h^1(C, 𝒪(D)) = ℓ(K - D)` for a canonical divisor `K`
(see [St09, Sections 1.5, 1.6]). -/
noncomputable def indexOfSpeciality (D : Divisor F) : ℤ :=
  D.ell - D.deg + genus F - 1

/-- A divisor `K` is *canonical* if `deg K = 2g - 2` and `ℓ(K) ≥ g`; equivalently, `K` is the
divisor of a nonzero rational differential on the curve (see [St09, Section 1.6]). -/
def IsCanonical (K : Divisor F) : Prop :=
  K.deg = 2 * (genus F : ℤ) - 2 ∧ genus F ≤ K.ell

variable (F) in
/-- The curve is *hyperelliptic* if it has genus `g ≥ 2` and admits a divisor `D` with
`deg D = 2` and `ℓ(D) = 2`, i.e. a degree two map to `ℙ¹` (see [St09, Section 6.2]). -/
def IsHyperelliptic : Prop :=
  2 ≤ genus F ∧ ∃ D : Divisor F, D.deg = 2 ∧ D.ell = 2

variable (F) in
/-- The *Clifford index* of the curve with function field `F` (of genus `g ≥ 4`):
`Cliff(C) = min {deg D - 2 (ℓ(D) - 1) | h^0(D) ≥ 2 and h^1(D) ≥ 2}`, where `h^0(D) = ℓ(D)` and
`h^1(D) = i(D)` is the index of speciality. By Clifford's theorem each such
`deg D - 2 (ℓ(D) - 1)` is a nonnegative integer. -/
noncomputable def cliffordIndex : ℕ :=
  sInf {c : ℕ | ∃ D : Divisor F, 2 ≤ D.ell ∧ 2 ≤ indexOfSpeciality D ∧
    (c : ℤ) = D.deg - 2 * (D.ell - 1)}

/-- The exterior algebra `⋀_F (F ⊗_ℂ V)` with `V = 𝓛(K)`; the Koszul complex computing the Koszul
cohomology groups `K_{p,q}(C, K)` lives inside it. -/
abbrev KoszulSpace (K : Divisor F) :=
  ExteriorAlgebra F (F ⊗[ℂ] K.riemannRochSpace)

/-- The Koszul differential: contraction against the `F`-linear form
`F ⊗_ℂ 𝓛(K) → F`, `f ⊗ v ↦ f v`. On `w • (v₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ vₙ)` it is
`∑ᵢ (-1)^(i+1) (vᵢ w) • (v₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ v̂ᵢ ∧ ⋯ ∧ vₙ)`. -/
noncomputable def koszulDifferential (K : Divisor F) : KoszulSpace K →ₗ[ℂ] KoszulSpace K :=
  (CliffordAlgebra.contractLeft (Q := (0 : QuadraticForm F (F ⊗[ℂ] K.riemannRochSpace)))
    (K.riemannRochSpace.subtype.liftBaseChange F)).restrictScalars ℂ

@[category API, AMS 13 14]
theorem koszulDifferential_comp_self (K : Divisor F) :
    koszulDifferential K ∘ₗ koszulDifferential K = 0 := by
  ext x
  simp [koszulDifferential, CliffordAlgebra.contractLeft_contractLeft]

@[category test, AMS 13 14]
theorem koszulDifferential_smul_ιMulti_one (K : Divisor F) (w : F) (v : K.riemannRochSpace) :
    koszulDifferential K (w • ExteriorAlgebra.ιMulti F 1 (fun _ => (1 : F) ⊗ₜ[ℂ] v)) =
      algebraMap F _ (w * v) := by
  simp [koszulDifferential, ExteriorAlgebra.ιMulti_apply, Algebra.smul_def]
  rw [CliffordAlgebra.contractLeft_algebraMap_mul, CliffordAlgebra.contractLeft_ι]
  simp

@[category test, AMS 13 14]
theorem koszulDifferential_ιMulti_two (K : Divisor F) (v₁ v₂ : K.riemannRochSpace) :
    koszulDifferential K
      (ExteriorAlgebra.ιMulti F 2 ![(1 : F) ⊗ₜ[ℂ] v₁, (1 : F) ⊗ₜ[ℂ] v₂]) =
      (v₁ : F) • ExteriorAlgebra.ι F ((1 : F) ⊗ₜ[ℂ] v₂) -
        (v₂ : F) • ExteriorAlgebra.ι F ((1 : F) ⊗ₜ[ℂ] v₁) := by
  simp [koszulDifferential, ExteriorAlgebra.ιMulti_apply, CliffordAlgebra.contractLeft_ι_mul,
    CliffordAlgebra.contractLeft_ι, Algebra.smul_def, Algebra.commutes]

/-- The bigraded piece `⋀^p V ⊗_ℂ W` of the Koszul complex, for `V = 𝓛(K)` and a `ℂ`-subspace
`W ⊆ F`: the `ℂ`-span of the elements `w • (v₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ vₚ)` with `w ∈ W` and `vᵢ ∈ V`. -/
def koszulPiece (K : Divisor F) (p : ℕ) (W : Submodule ℂ F) : Submodule ℂ (KoszulSpace K) :=
  Submodule.span ℂ {x | ∃ (w : F) (v : Fin p → K.riemannRochSpace), w ∈ W ∧
    x = w • ExteriorAlgebra.ιMulti F p (fun i => (1 : F) ⊗ₜ[ℂ] v i)}

/-- The Koszul cohomology group `K_{p,q}(C, K)` vanishes: the cycles in `⋀^p V ⊗ 𝓛(qK)` are
exactly the boundaries of `⋀^(p+1) V ⊗ 𝓛((q-1)K)`, where `V = 𝓛(K)`. When `K` is canonical
and the curve is non-hyperelliptic, `K_{p,q}(C, K) = 0` means that the graded Betti number
`β_{p,p+q}` of the canonical curve vanishes. -/
def KoszulCohomologyVanishes (K : Divisor F) (p q : ℕ) : Prop :=
  LinearMap.ker (koszulDifferential K) ⊓ koszulPiece K p ((q : ℤ) • K).riemannRochSpace =
    (koszulPiece K (p + 1) (((q : ℤ) - 1) • K).riemannRochSpace).map (koszulDifferential K)

variable (F) in
/-- **Green's conjecture.** Let $C$ be a smooth projective non-hyperelliptic curve over
$\mathbb{C}$ of genus $g \ge 4$, with function field $F$ and canonical divisor $K$. Then the
Clifford index of $C$ is determined by the linear syzygies of the canonical curve
$C \subseteq \mathbb{P}^{g-1}$:
$$\operatorname{Cliff}(C) = \min\{p : K_{p,2}(C, K_C) \neq 0\},$$
i.e. $K_{p,2}(C, K_C) = 0$ for all $p < \operatorname{Cliff}(C)$ and
$K_{\operatorname{Cliff}(C), 2}(C, K_C) \ne 0$. Equivalently, if $a(C)$ is the largest $i$ such that
the graded Betti numbers $\beta_{p,p+2}$ of the canonical curve vanish for all $p \le i$, then
$\operatorname{Cliff}(C) = a(C) + 1$. The inequality $a(C) + 1 \le \operatorname{Cliff}(C)$ is the
Green–Lazarsfeld nonvanishing theorem; the reverse inequality is the open part.

The hypothesis $g \ge 4$ excludes the degenerate cases: curves of genus $g \le 2$ are
hyperelliptic (or have no canonical embedding), and a non-hyperelliptic curve of genus $3$ is a
plane quartic, for which no divisor computes the Clifford index and $K_{p,2}(C, K_C) = 0$ for
all $p$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 13 14]
theorem greens_conjecture [Algebra (RatFunc ℂ) F] [IsScalarTower ℂ (RatFunc ℂ) F]
    [FunctionField ℂ F]
    (hg : 4 ≤ genus F) (hC : ¬ IsHyperelliptic F) (K : Divisor F) (hK : IsCanonical K) :
    IsLeast {p : ℕ | ¬ KoszulCohomologyVanishes K p 2} (cliffordIndex F) := by
  sorry

end GreensConjecture

items: Curve ↔ function field: a smooth projective curve C over ℂ is modelled (up to isomorphism, which is all the conjecture depends on) by its function field F, formalised with Mathlib's `FunctionField ℂ F` (= `FiniteDimensional (RatFunc ℂ) F`) together with `[Algebra ℂ F] [Algebra (RatFunc ℂ) F] [IsScalarTower ℂ (RatFunc ℂ) F]`. Since ℂ is algebraically closed the constant field is exactly ℂ.

Places (closed points) are valuation subrings 𝒪 ⊊ F containing ℂ (Stichtenoth's definition). The DVR property and residue field ℂ are theorems, not imposed; a reviewer should confirm no extra/missing points result (Stichtenoth Thm 1.1.6 / Prop 1.1.15).

Uniformizer at P := generator of the maximal ideal of 𝒪_P. Riemann–Roch space 𝓛(D) := {f | ∀ P, ∀ uniformizers t at P, t^{D(P)}·f ∈ 𝒪_P}, encoding v_P(f) ≥ −D(P) without an explicit ℤ-valued valuation; independence of the choice of uniformizer makes the ∀ harmless. ℓ(D) := finrank; 𝓛(D) is finite-dimensional mathematically, so Lean's junk value 0 for infinite dimension is never reached.
Degree of a divisor is the sum of coefficients (all places have degree 1 over ℂ).
Genus defined via Riemann's theorem as sSup {deg D − ℓ(D) + 1} in ℕ (Stichtenoth's Def. of genus). The set contains 0 (D = 0) and is bounded above by g, so ℕ's sSup is the maximum.

Canonical divisors are defined by the numerical characterisation deg K = 2g − 2 ∧ ℓ(K) ≥ g (Stichtenoth Prop. 1.6.2), rather than via Kähler differentials, to avoid unprovable side conditions in definitions. The theorem quantifies over all canonical K (all statements involved are invariant under linear equivalence).
h^1(D) is taken as the index of speciality i(D) = ℓ(D) − deg D + g − 1 (equal to ℓ(K − D) by Riemann–Roch / Serre duality).

Clifford index := sInf over ℕ of {deg D − 2(ℓ(D) − 1) : ℓ(D) ≥ 2, i(D) ≥ 2}. Values are ≥ 0 by Clifford's theorem, and for g ≥ 4 the set is nonempty (a gonality pencil contributes), so sInf is the true minimum; casts are placed at the leaves (checked).
Non-hyperelliptic := ¬(g ≥ 2 ∧ ∃ D, deg D = 2 ∧ ℓ(D) = 2) (Stichtenoth Def. 6.2.1, valid over ℂ).

Koszul cohomology K_{p,q}(C,K_C) is realised inside the exterior algebra ⋀_F(F ⊗_ℂ V), V = 𝓛(K) ≅ H^0(C,K_C), with differential the contraction `CliffordAlgebra.contractLeft` against f ⊗ v ↦ f·v (test lemmas verify d(w·v) = w v and d(v₁∧v₂) = v₁v₂ − v₂v₁, and d∘d = 0). The bigraded piece ⋀^p V ⊗ 𝓛(qK) is the ℂ-span of w • (v₁∧…∧v_p); 'K_{p,q} = 0' is stated as equality of ℂ-submodules: cycles in ⋀^p V ⊗ 𝓛(qK) = d(⋀^{p+1} V ⊗ 𝓛((q−1)K)). This uses the identification ⋀_F(F⊗_ℂ V) ≅ F ⊗_ℂ ⋀_ℂ V and injectivity of W ⊗ ⋀^p V → F ⊗ ⋀^p V for W ⊆ F.

The Betti-number formulation (β_{p,p+2} of the canonical curve) equals dim K_{p,2}(C,K_C) because the canonical ring is the homogeneous coordinate ring for non-hyperelliptic curves (Noether's theorem); the file states Green's original Koszul-cohomology form.

Genus restricted to g ≥ 4 and equality expressed as `IsLeast`: for g = 3 non-hyperelliptic (plane quartic) all β_{p,p+2} vanish, so a(C) is undefined and the equality form is meaningless (Cliff = 1 only by convention), while the open content is trivially true there; and the naive 'K_{p,2} = 0 ⟺ p < Cliff for all p' is false for p ≥ g − 2 (where K_{p,2} = 0 always), so the faithful reading is Cliff(C) = min{p : K_{p,2} ≠ 0}, which `IsLeast` states (its 'membership' half is the Green–Lazarsfeld theorem, its 'lower bound' half is the open part).

reviewer_notes: Source ambiguities: (1) The Wikipedia gloss 'a(C) = largest i with β_{i,i+2} = 0' must be read as 'β_{p,p+2} = 0 for all p ≤ i'; and 'K_{p,2} = 0 ⟺ p < Cliff' (decomposition notes) is false for p ≥ g−2 where K_{p,2} vanishes trivially — the correct form Cliff = min{p : K_{p,2} ≠ 0} is what the final file states. (2) Wikipedia's Clifford-index phrasing 'min over special divisors except canonical and trivial' is sloppy (a single point would give ≤ 1); the standard definition (h⁰ ≥ 2, h¹ ≥ 2), used by all candidates and by Green–Lazarsfeld, is the intended one. (3) The statement is stated for genus ≥ 4: at g = 3 (plane quartics) the equality Cliff = a(C)+1 fails under the standard convention Cliff = 1 (all β_{p,p+2} vanish), so the restriction is a necessary correction and loses no open content; it is documented in the theorem docstring. The bail-outs (c01, c02, c04, c05) are right that Mathlib lacks curves/genus/Koszul cohomology, but the four filed candidates show these can be built faithfully from Mathlib primitives (valuation subrings/valuations, Finsupp, finrank, exterior algebra with `CliffordAlgebra.contractLeft`, tensor products) without placeholders, so rejection is not warranted. The final file includes the proven Green–Lazarsfeld direction (K_{Cliff,2} ≠ 0) as part of the equality, matching the source's 'equality always holds'; the open content is K_{p,2} = 0 for p < Cliff. The bespoke definitions live in the problem file; a maintainer may prefer moving the generic curve/function-field ones to FormalConjecturesForMathlib. The final file passes `lake --wfail build` with the repository's linters.
statement: Green's conjecture: the Clifford index of a non-hyperelliptic curve is determined by the extent to which it, as a canonical curve, has linear syzygies.
